title: Pinot in Champagne
subtitle: Black grapes, white wine
objectives: Explain Pinot Noir's role in Champagne

steps.title: Structure and body
steps.body: Pinot Noir is about 38% of Champagne's vineyards, the most planted grape there. It gives body, structure and red fruit aromas to blends. The Montagne de Reims, with Grand Crus like Aÿ, Bouzy and Verzenay, and the Côte des Bar, in the south, are its strongholds.

steps.title: White from black
steps.body: Since the colour is in the skins, gentle pressing of whole bunches gives a pale, white juice from black grapes. Blanc de Noirs is white Champagne made only from Pinot Noir and/or Meunier. It's fuller and fruitier than Blanc de Blancs. For rosé Champagne, a little still red Pinot Noir is often blended in.
steps.highlight: Blanc de Noirs: white from black

steps.prompt: How can Champagne make white wine from Pinot Noir?
options: By gentle pressing that keeps the colour out
steps.explanation: Colour is in the skins; gentle whole-bunch pressing keeps it out of the juice.

steps.title: Still Pinot
steps.body: Bouzy, in the Montagne de Reims, is famous for still red wine, sold as Coteaux Champenois rouge. In warmer years, more producers make it. Its light, crisp style shows Pinot Noir at the edge of ripeness, a reminder of how cool Champagne is.

steps.prompt: Pinot Noir is the most planted grape in Champagne.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Pinot Noir is Champagne's most planted grape, giving body
Blanc de Noirs is white Champagne from black grapes
Bouzy makes still red Coteaux Champenois
